title: Anti-concentration for $B$-reasonable variables
statement:
Let $X$ be a real-valued random variable on a probability space $(\Omega, P)$ with finite second and fourth moments and $\E[X^2] > 0$, and suppose $X$ is $B$-reasonable. Then for every $t \in [0,1]$,
\[
P\bigl(\,\abs{X} > t\,\norm{X}_2\,\bigr) \ge \frac{(1-t^2)^2}{B},
\]
where $\norm{X}_2 = \bigl(\E[X^2]\bigr)^{1/2}$; equivalently, the probability that $X^2 > t^2\,\E[X^2]$ is at least $(1-t^2)^2/B$.
hypotheses_covered: X is B-reasonable (fourth moment controlled by squared second moment)
second moment E[X^2] is finite (X^2 integrable)
fourth moment E[X^4] is finite (X^4 integrable)
replaced:
If $X$ is $B$-reasonable and not equivalent to $0$, then for every $t \in [0,1]$,
\[
\Pr\bigl[\,|X| > t\,\norm{X}_2\,\bigr] \ge \frac{(1-t^2)^2}{B}.
\]
